analysis.title: Weekly commentary: AI: looking beyond the buildout (Nov. 16, 2026)
key_insights: BlackRock keeps a strategic (5+ year) overweight in U.S. equities on conviction in AI's improving capabilities and adoption, while it downgraded U.S. stocks tactically to neutral last month and advises near-term caution.
The conviction does not rely on today's earnings growth or on current AI winners staying on top. The starting-point scenario sees valuations declining without assuming a permanent growth breakout.

U.S. valuation depends on the measure: the Shiller CAPE is 40.7x, near dot-com highs, while the 12-month forward P/E is 18.8x and looks less stretched only because investors expect strong earnings growth.

Key AI uncertainty is how the buildout evolves relative to demand and adoption. Falling computing costs could squeeze suppliers' profits, and bottlenecks could delay adoption. Both could cause near-term pressure without necessarily undermining the longer-term opportunity.
Overcapacity is a risk, and builders' earnings could slow before adopters see meaningful gains. BlackRock describes a 'polyfurcated' environment where multiple scenarios are plausible.

Strategic overweight in U.S. equities is supported by longer-term earnings prospects in U.S. health care, IT, tech and financials, and is a key driver of the broader developed-market equity overweight.

AI buildout financing competes with heavy government borrowing for the same pool of savings. BlackRock revised up its interest rate expectations in its capital market assumptions and expects policy rates to stay elevated for longer on a higher neutral rate.

For the first time since 2020, BlackRock is more constructive on duration risk: it moved to neutral on developed-market government bonds and strengthened its overweight in inflation-linked bonds, though government bonds are no longer all-weather diversifiers.

U.S. stocks recovered nearly all post-midterm election losses last week, the S&P 500's best week since early August, led by chips (Philadelphia Semiconductor index +8%). AI earnings optimism is outweighing higher rates for now.
Two-year U.S. Treasury yields rose 33 basis points to 4.86% after hawkish Fed comments and a hotter-than-expected inflation report.

Tactical positioning (6-12 months): neutral U.S., Europe, UK, Japan and China equities, overweight emerging market equities (strong earnings, cheaper valuations, AI scarcity theme in Asia and Latin America).

Fixed income tactical views: overweight short-term U.S. Treasuries (much of anticipated repricing has occurred, expectations of further Fed hikes look excessive), neutral long-term Treasuries (yields could still rise), underweight Japanese government bonds and long-term IG credit, overweight emerging local currency debt.

Week ahead focus is on European and Japanese inflation data for signs that higher energy costs are broadening price pressures, potentially prompting further rate hikes, plus European consumer confidence.

tension_points.bear_case: Overcapacity, falling computing costs squeezing suppliers' profits and adoption bottlenecks could cause near-term pressure, and builders' earnings could slow before adopters see gains.
